lessons: Verify material_type / availability_type / publication_year_from params against a live residential-IP NLI call next cycle (NLI docs are Cloudflare-blocked from datacenter IPs).

cycles.trigger: Batch2 drift-type-C review: external-site dependency, link rot, and the lowest trust score in the batch (71).
changes: CLOSED the carried lesson from 1.1.0. The NLI docs are Cloudflare-blocked live, but both pages are readable on web.archive.org. Verified the clause grammar, the filters/commands lists, the three-character minimum, the Errors-header behaviour and the documented attribute list against the captures, and repointed nine evidence rows from the 403ing live URLs to the captures so they now verify.
Added `shelfmark`, which is a documented query attribute the skill never listed.

NEW CARRY: `subject` appears in NO published NLI attribute list or example, yet it leads most of this skill's examples. Combined with silent condition-dropping, an unrecognised attribute returns UNFILTERED results that look like a successful topical search. Added a gotcha telling the agent to inspect the Errors header and fall back to title/creator.

CORRECTED gotcha 6. The Cloudflare block is triggered by the User-Agent, not by a datacenter IP: verified that the same request from the same machine gets an HTML challenge with no UA or curl's default, and structured JSON with any ordinary UA.

REPLACED the Troubleshooting 403 row. It asserted 'the key may be invalid or expired' for every 403, which is a guessed cause the agent quotes verbatim. Verified live that the API distinguishes API_KEY_MISSING, API_KEY_INVALID and OVER_RATE_LIMIT in the JSON body, and that a Cloudflare block is HTML. Replaced with a body-based decision table.
Added NLI's own published guest API key, which the skill previously deferred to a third-party MCP for, plus the honest caveat that it returns 429 OVER_RATE_LIMIT in practice.

FIXED THE EXECUTABILITY INVARIANT. metadata.json declares chatgpt, claude-ai, claude-desktop and manus; none can run the bundled script and three cannot run a local stdio MCP, so four of eleven declared hosts had NO data path. Added an explicit two-route table with a browser route via the public catalogue.

Added three coverage sections the skill was silent on: that NLI is not the right archive for state, Zionist-institutional, military or municipal records; how to actually cite an NLI item (shelfmark and system number, both already in the response); and that reuse rights differ item by item and must not be implied.
Made availability_type prominent: a catalogue record is not a scan, and this is the parameter that separates them.
Documented that `contains` on a date is a substring match, not a range, a defect inherited from NLI's own worked example.

REFRAMED references/historical-periods.md as an explicit search-term guide rather than a historical reference, and fixed the British Mandate 1917-1948 boundary (1917 is the Ottoman defeat and Balfour; civil Mandate administration began in 1920). Hedged the aliyah-wave ranges as conventions. Added Arabic and alternative-name search terms throughout, which is a RECALL fix before it is anything else: NLI holds Arabic-language material on the same events and a single-vocabulary term list cannot retrieve it.

Removed the unverifiable '30,000+ maps' figure for the Eran Laor collection and corrected the collection name. Replaced the 'Shapell Archive' row, which pointed at a digitisation project rather than a holding, with JPress, and added a caution about collection names generally.
Corrected the Schwadron and Manuscripts entries, and separated the Manuscripts Collection from the IMHM, which holds surrogates of manuscripts owned elsewhere.

scripts/nli-search-example.py: added error handling (it previously dumped a raw Python traceback on the single most common failure, a bad key), surfaced the Errors response header as a warning, handled a non-list response shape, added --guest, and gave an actionable empty-result message. All three error paths exercised live against the real API.

Expert/Judge round 2 fixes: corrected the Cloudflare claim again after the Judge falsified my own test (a bare `curl` with no -A still sends curl/x.y.z, so my 'no User-Agent' case was never tested; a raw-socket probe with the header genuinely absent reaches the API cleanly, so the rule targets the curl signature specifically).

Removed the script's --from-year/--to-year pair. It ANDed two substring clauses, asking for a date string containing BOTH years, which matches almost nothing, while the docstring advertised it as a range search. Replaced with a single --year and an explicit note that there is no range query.

Fixed references/historical-periods.md recommending material_type values `audio` and `videos`, which the skill's own gotcha 4 lists as invalid and silently dropped, so following the reference produced an UNFILTERED result set presented as a filtered one.
Propagated the Mandate 1917/1920 correction and the removal of an unsourced 'NLI holds Ottoman-era land records' claim into SKILL.md's period tips; both had landed only in the Hebrew file.
Added the null-result rule to both files: an empty result set does not prove absence, because the API searches catalogued records only. Added a required Search Limits section to the report template.

Reconciled the empty-result remedy with gotcha 7: recommending `subject,contains` as the fix for zero results was recommending the one attribute that may be silently dropped and return falsely full results.
Made the output templates and the script formatter actually emit the citation the new citation rule specifies (creator, holding institution, shelfmark, system number, permalink, access and rights).
Moved the availability_type prose out of the middle of the parameter table in both files, where it was breaking every table row after it.
Added --online-only, --page and --count to the script, so it can express availability_type, page past the first page, and report a total match count.
Softened the `subject` gotcha to UNCONFIRMED: the archived source names the filterable attributes but describes the text side as open-ended, so 'documented absent' over-read it.
Updated metadata.json display_description, which promised unconditional search on hosts that cannot search.

Hebrew quality pass on Expert findings (מסננים not פאסטים, סימן מדף not מספר המדף, and several English calques), and fixed a Hebrew example comment that labelled a 1917 substring match as 'the Mandate period', reintroducing the error the same file corrects.
Deleted a committed scripts/__pycache__ .pyc artifact.
deviations: Could not verify the Merhav deep-link query-string form: merhav.nli.org.il serves a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge that a headless browser cannot clear. The browser route is therefore documented as 'drive it through the interface', with the host named but no deep link published as working.
Could not source a replacement figure for the Laor collection size, so no number is stated rather than swapping one unverified figure for another.
Could not test the `subject` attribute live: the shared guest key is rate-exhausted and I have no personal key.
lessons: CARRY (was: verify params against a live call): now narrowed and still open. Test whether `subject` is a recognised attribute with a real keyed call, and inspect the Errors header. This is the only remaining correctness risk in the parameter tables and it affects most of the skill's examples.
CARRY: confirm the Merhav deep-link URL form from a real browser session so Route B can publish a working example query.
CARRY: verify the Eran Laor collection size and the current official collection names on nli.org.il.

METHOD, and this is the important one: the evidence gate extracts ZERO numeric facts from this skill. Every run reports '0 facts, N URLs' and exits clean. Bare years, the aliyah-wave ranges and the '30,000+ maps' figure were never checked by any gate, in either direction, across two cycles. For a skill whose factual surface is dates and collection sizes rather than currency amounts, the gate is decorative and the only real check is a human reading the sources. Do not treat a green gate on this skill as evidence of anything.
CARRY: the script still does not escape a comma inside a user-supplied value, so a creator string containing a comma is indistinguishable from a clause delimiter.
CARRY: --lang is unvalidated free text while --type and --sort are constrained, so a bad language code is exactly the silently-dropped-condition case.
CARRY: the IIIF Presentation (manifest) API is a Should-cover checklist item and is still only half covered; there is no procedure for reading canvases out of a manifest.
CARRY: Route B is executable by the USER in a browser, not by the assistant, on the four hosts it was written for. The text should say so plainly.
CARRY: historical-periods.md still gives intifada and Oslo dates as bare parentheticals under a banner telling the reader not to treat dates as fact.

METHOD: a reviewer falsified my own empirical claim this cycle and was right. `curl` without -A is not a request without a User-Agent. When testing what triggers a bot rule, control the header explicitly at the socket level rather than trusting a CLI's defaults.

cycles.trigger: Release blocker raised after v1.2.0 shipped: unverified `subject` attribute must not remain in worked examples.
changes: REMOVED every `subject` clause from the skill. All worked examples, the collections-table recipes and the reference curl examples now use documented attributes (title, creator, publisher, language, start_date, shelfmark, system_number). The attribute-table row for `subject` is struck through and explains why.
Removed the Troubleshooting recommendation to fall back to `subject,contains` on empty results, which could convert a zero-result search into a falsely full one.

Downgraded Route B from an implied endpoint to explicit user-executed instructions: merhav.nli.org.il and www.nli.org.il sit behind a Cloudflare interstitial that a headless browser does not clear and that took about twelve seconds even in an interactive session. The skill now tells the agent to hand the user search terms and steps rather than presenting a URL it can call.
deviations: Could not obtain an NLI API key to settle `subject` empirically. The shared guest key remains rate-exhausted (429 OVER_RATE_LIMIT on retry) and the signup form requires a real name, email address and acceptance of terms, which is not mine to submit. Per the release instruction the examples came out rather than shipping with a caveat, because the failure mode is invisible at the point of use.
lessons: CARRY: settle `subject` with one live keyed call. If it IS supported, restore it as the primary topical attribute; if not, this removal is permanent. Highest-value open question on this skill.

METHOD: a caveat is not a mitigation when the failure is silent. An unrecognised attribute returns a populated result set that ignored the topic, so a warning in the docs cannot reach a user who never sees an error. Removing the construct was the only safe option while it was unverified.
